answer: Beacon-Beam Registration. Each agent periodically emits a routing beacon signed with its key; peers record the beam path (which nodes relayed it) in a local orchard of recent routes. A new identity is admitted only if its beacon traverses at least three distinct, previously independent relay neighborhoods — a sparse meadow of verified paths. Attackers must physically position each sybil across separate relay clusters, paying real bandwidth, latency, and relay-node maintenance per identity rather than a one-time fee.
